items.headline: Kaprizov brings NHL-high 13 goals into Wild–Mammoth
items.summary: Kirill Kaprizov is three goals shy of Mario Lemieux's record for goals in a single October (16) and four points from 500 for his career as Minnesota visits Utah in a top-of-the-Central meeting.

items.headline: Colts agree to send Quenton Nelson to Seahawks
items.summary: Indianapolis is trading the veteran guard, in the last year of his contract, to Seattle for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder, per multiple reports.

items.headline: Cowboys rout Eagles 38–21 on Monday Night Football
items.summary: Dak Prescott threw three touchdowns, two to CeeDee Lamb, and Javonte Williams ran for 155 yards in Philadelphia. Dallas moves to 3-4 and the Eagles fall to 2-5.

items.headline: Hellebuyck projected to make Devils debut in Dallas
items.summary: Connor Hellebuyck, acquired from Winnipeg on Oct. 23, is the projected starter for New Jersey against a Stars team that has won five straight; Jason Robertson has four straight multipoint games.

items.headline: Canadiens without Suzuki at St. Louis
items.summary: Nick Suzuki (upper body) is listed as injured along with Ivan Demidov and Samuel Montembeault; Jordan Binnington starts for the Blues for the first time since Oct. 17.

items.headline: Flames beat Maple Leafs 5–2 for first time since 2022
items.summary: Matvei Gridin scored twice, once on the power play, and Mikael Backlund added a goal as Calgary topped Toronto; William Nylander and Easton Cowan scored for the Leafs.

items.headline: Red Wings rally, win in shootout at Edmonton
items.summary: Dylan Larkin tied it 3–3 with 1:17 left in regulation and Lucas Raymond scored the only shootout goal as Detroit won 4–3.

items.headline: Kings end Rangers' home win streak 6–3
items.summary: Los Angeles scored six on Madison Square Garden ice; Tye Kartye scored twice and Adam Fox once for New York. The Kings play again tonight in Chicago.

items.headline: League-leading Bruins visit Hurricanes; Hall returns
items.summary: Boston (9-2-1) is 7-0-1 in its last eight and leads the NHL at +22; Carolina (9-2-2) gets Taylor Hall back from an upper-body injury, while Jordan Staal remains out.

items.headline: McCaffrey says he'll be 'alright' after thigh injury
items.summary: The 49ers running back briefly left Sunday's loss to Atlanta with a thigh injury before returning; rookie Kaelon Black scored his first NFL touchdown in his absence.

items.headline: Canadiens edge Jets 2–1 in Heritage Classic
items.summary: Jacob Fowler made 33 saves outdoors in Winnipeg as Lane Hutson and Kaiden Guhle scored in the second period; Isak Rosen's late goal was Winnipeg's only reply in its first game since trading Connor Hellebuyck.

items.headline: Seahawks hold Chiefs to a field goal in 20–3 Sunday night win
items.summary: Seattle's defence smothered Kansas City, but the Seahawks lost receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) during the game; early reports on him are positive.

items.headline: Quinn Hughes scores in Vancouver return as Wild win 4–2
items.summary: Hughes had a goal and an assist, reaching 500 career points, and Kirill Kaprizov added his league-leading 13th goal plus an assist; Vancouver's losing streak continues.

items.headline: Seahawks LT Charles Cross has high ankle sprain; Packers C Sean Rhyan likely the same
items.summary: Seattle hopes Cross misses only one to two weeks. Green Bay's Rhyan had negative X-rays and an MRI scheduled Monday after the loss in Detroit.

items.headline: O'Reilly and Stamkos score twice each as Predators rout Avalanche 6–2
items.summary: Nashville scored four power-play goals, two of them by O'Reilly; Roman Josi had three assists and Martin Necas two for Colorado.

items.headline: Panthers lose OT Taylor Moton to fractured fibula
items.summary: Moton was hurt in the 43–13 loss to Tampa Bay and coach Dave Canales said he will be out for a while.

items.headline: Rangers sign James Reimer; he's expected to start tonight vs. Kings
items.summary: With Igor Shesterkin and Joonas Korpisalo both hurt, the 38-year-old signed a one-year deal Sunday and is expected to make his first Rangers start against Los Angeles.

items.headline: Raiders weighing changes after fourth straight loss
items.summary: After a 35–21 home loss to the Rams dropped Las Vegas to 3-4, coach Klint Kubiak said the team is considering everything, including more snaps for rookie Fernando Mendoza.

items.headline: Robertson scores twice as Stars beat Islanders 6–3 for fifth straight win
items.summary: Jason Robertson extended his multipoint streak to four games, and Dallas scored a season-high six goals.

items.headline: Lions edge Packers 20–17; Vikings improve to 6-0
items.summary: Detroit held on at Ford Field, and Minnesota beat Indianapolis 16–10, though RB Aaron Jones left with a knee injury and is day to day.

items.headline: Maple Leafs rout Oilers 7–2 for fourth straight win
items.summary: Stolarz made 30 saves and Nylander scored twice in Edmonton. Draisaitl's two goals stretched his goal streak to six games and McDavid's two assists kept his season-opening point streak alive at 11.

items.headline: Jets send Connor Hellebuyck to the Devils
items.summary: Winnipeg dealt the goalie to New Jersey for Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws, Alexander Command, Nick Bjugstad and two picks after his camp holdout. No debut date has been set.

items.headline: Canadiens and Jets meet outdoors in the Heritage Classic tonight
items.summary: Winnipeg's Elias Salomonsson makes his season debut after April shoulder surgery, while Montreal plays without captain Nick Suzuki.

items.headline: Stars rule out Sam Steel; David Perron could debut vs. Islanders
items.summary: Steel is out after an injection Friday and Radek Faksa is a game-time call. Perron, 38, signed Oct. 16 and may play his first game for Dallas.

items.headline: Titans without Calvin Ridley and Tyjae Spears against Browns
items.summary: Tennessee's receiver and backup running back are inactive. Cleveland cornerback Denzel Ward is active.

items.headline: Breece Hall inactive as Jets face Dolphins
items.summary: New York also sits guard Dylan Parham and edge Joseph Ossai; Miami is without linebacker Willie Gay Jr. and receiver Jalen Tolbert.

items.headline: Eagles' DeVonta Smith misses Saturday practice; Barkley back on field
items.summary: Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were not seen at practice, while Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert took part.

items.headline: Browns activate RB Dylan Sampson from injured reserve
items.summary: Cleveland brought Sampson (knee) back Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans.

items.headline: Jets trade Connor Hellebuyck to the Devils
items.summary: Winnipeg ends the summer-long saga by sending the three-time Vezina winner to New Jersey for a package including Dawson Mercer, Nico Daws, Nick Bjugstad and picks. He will not play Saturday against the Kings and has no set debut date.

items.headline: Lamar Jackson questionable for Ravens against Bengals
items.summary: Jackson (ankle) has missed the past two games but says he is heading in the right direction; Baltimore also lost LB Tavius Robinson for the season.

items.headline: Bears place Cole Kmet on injured reserve with season-ending knee injury
items.summary: Ben Johnson confirmed the tight end was hurt in Chicago's win over New England.

items.headline: Tavares week to week as Maple Leafs visit Edmonton
items.summary: Toronto is also without Nick Blankenburg and Marshall Rifai; Edmonton is missing Mattias Ekholm for one to two weeks and put Devon Levi on IR.

items.headline: Jaguars' Anton Harrison and Giants' Tremaine Edmunds lost for the season
items.summary: Harrison's torn ACL was found during knee surgery; Edmunds has a torn chest muscle.

items.headline: MacKinnon has a goal and three assists as Avalanche beat Lightning 6–3
items.summary: Necas added a goal and two assists and Blackwood made 31 saves; Jake Guentzel scored twice for Tampa Bay.

items.headline: Kucherov held off the scoresheet, still tied with Stamkos for Tampa Bay's points record
items.summary: Kucherov sits at 1,137 career points, one away from becoming the Lightning's all-time leader; Tampa Bay plays at Utah tonight on a back-to-back.

items.headline: Jake Evans scores twice as Canadiens beat Blackhawks 4–1
items.summary: Evans had two goals and an assist, including a shorthanded goal; Fowler made 20 saves and Connor Bedard scored Chicago's only goal.

items.headline: Saturday: 12 games, with Oilers hosting Maple Leafs
items.summary: McDavid (31 points in 10 games) faces Toronto's 97.4% penalty kill; Jarry starts for Edmonton.

items.headline: Goalie news: Johansson starts for Ottawa, Postava likely for Detroit
items.summary: Jonas Johansson makes his first start of the season against the Rangers; Detroit is expected to turn to Michal Postava in Calgary.

items.headline: Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki out 2-4 weeks
items.summary: An upper-body injury ends Suzuki's 546-game ironman streak, second-longest active in the NHL. Oliver Kapanen moved between Caufield and Slafkovsky at practice.

items.headline: Bears hold off Patriots 30–24 on Thursday Night Football
items.summary: Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in his return from a hamstring injury, and Luther Burden III had 130 receiving yards, all in the first half. Chicago is 5-2.

items.headline: Rams' Myles Garrett could return to practice next week
items.summary: Out since Week 1 after knee surgery, Garrett is ruled out against the Raiders but could return to practice the week of Oct. 26, with Week 8 against the Chargers possible.

items.headline: Bears TE Cole Kmet headed to injured reserve with a knee injury
items.summary: Ben Johnson called the right-knee injury serious and said Kmet will go on IR; reports say it is likely season-ending, pending tests.

items.headline: McDavid and Draisaitl each post five points as Oilers outlast Hurricanes 6–5 in a shootout
items.summary: Both stars had two goals and three assists; Edmonton scored three power-play goals and rallied with three in the third period.

items.headline: Sharks rout Senators 6–2 behind two shorthanded goals
items.summary: San Jose scored twice shorthanded and twice into an empty net despite being outshot 43–28; Yaroslav Askarov was named first star.

items.headline: Lucas Raymond scores twice as Red Wings beat Canucks 5–2
items.summary: Raymond had two goals and an assist on five shots, and Detroit outshot Vancouver 31–13.

items.headline: Shutouts in Pittsburgh and Boston
items.summary: The Penguins blanked the Panthers 4–0 and the Bruins beat the Predators 6–0.

items.headline: Flames edge Wild 2–1 despite being outshot 37–22
items.summary: Calgary scored twice on the power play in the first period; Matt Boldy had seven shots and Kirill Kaprizov four without scoring.

items.headline: Tonight: Kucherov one point from Lightning franchise record in Colorado
items.summary: Kucherov (1,137 points) is tied with Steven Stamkos for Tampa Bay's all-time lead, and MacKinnon is two points from 1,300 including playoffs. In Chicago, Ian Cole plays his 1,000th game as Bedard faces Montreal.

items.headline: Senators put Ullmark on injured reserve; Ersson starts against San Jose
items.summary: Linus Ullmark left Wednesday's win over Florida with a lower-body strain and is on IR. Samuel Ersson starts Thursday, and Jonas Johansson was recalled from Belleville to back him up.

items.headline: Jalen Hurts reportedly out for the season with blood clots
items.summary: The Eagles quarterback was reportedly diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and clots in his lungs and is being treated with blood thinners. The NFLPA has called for a full investigation.

items.headline: Senators beat Panthers 5-1 in Brady Tkachuk's return to Ottawa
items.summary: Tkachuk scored a power-play goal in his first game back in Ottawa, but Tim Stutzle, Claude Giroux, Shane Pinto, Warren Foegele and Stephen Halliday all scored for the Senators.

items.headline: Baker Mayfield on track to return from thumb injury against Carolina
items.summary: Mayfield was a full participant in practice Wednesday and said his dislocated thumb is strong enough to play. He will wear a protective glove developed with input from the Tampa Bay Rays' staff.

items.headline: Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki out 2-4 weeks with a hand injury
items.summary: Montreal says Suzuki will miss two to four weeks. Kasperi Kapanen moved between Cole Caufield and Juraj Slafkovsky at practice.

items.headline: Cole Knuble scores twice as Flyers win 3-1 in Buffalo
items.summary: Knuble had two goals and Trevor Zegras added a power-play goal; Dan Vladar made 27 saves on 28 shots. Jason Zucker scored Buffalo's only goal.

items.headline: Patriots visit Bears on Thursday Night Football
items.summary: Drake Maye has no injury designation after a full practice. New England has ruled out cornerbacks Carlton Davis III, Channing Canada and Karon Prunty, and Chicago is without running back Kyle Monangai.

items.headline: Cooper Black to make his NHL debut as Markstrom misses 1-2 weeks
items.summary: Florida will start Black in Pittsburgh on the second night of a back-to-back. In Edmonton, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins makes his season debut against Carolina.

items.headline: Penguins put Bryan Rust and Ben Kindel on injured reserve
items.summary: Pittsburgh recalled Rutger McGroarty and Chase Pietila from Wilkes-Barre/Scranton. Ottawa's Thomas Chabot is expected to miss one to two weeks.

items.headline: 12-game Thursday slate, led by DeBrincat and Kaprizov
items.summary: Twelve games are on tonight. Detroit visits Vancouver, which allows a league-high 33.7 shots per game, and Minnesota plays in Calgary. Florida and Ottawa are both on the second night of back-to-backs.

items.headline: Dahlin and Zucker return as Buffalo hosts Philadelphia
items.summary: Captain Rasmus Dahlin is back after missing three games with an upper-body injury, and Jason Zucker makes his season debut after sports hernia surgery. Dahlin rejoins the top power-play unit.

items.headline: Sanderson returns for Ottawa against Brady Tkachuk and the Panthers
items.summary: Jake Sanderson plays after missing eight straight games and was paired with Artem Zub at the morning skate; Thomas Chabot remains out 1-2 weeks.

items.headline: Terry McLaurin out for the season with a torn patellar tendon
items.summary: Washington's top receiver tore his patellar tendon and will miss the rest of the year.

items.headline: Celebrini scores twice, including the overtime winner, as the Sharks rally past Montreal
items.summary: San Jose came back from 3-1 down in the third period and won 4-3 on Celebrini's power-play goal in OT. Caufield, Suzuki and Slafkovsky scored for the Canadiens.

items.headline: Mike Evans aggravates his Achilles; status for Sunday unclear
items.summary: Evans left Monday's win over Washington after 3 catches for 94 yards. Kyle Shanahan reportedly doesn't see it as a long-term issue, but his availability against Atlanta isn't confirmed.

items.headline: Rams lose Davante Adams for 6 to 10 weeks
items.summary: Adams ruptured a hamstring against Arizona and went on injured reserve. Kicker Blake Grupe (torn ACL) and DT Poona Ford (triceps) are out for the season; the Rams signed Brandon McManus.

items.headline: DeBrincat's 300th goal forces overtime, but Seattle wins in a shootout
items.summary: DeBrincat tied it 3-3 with 17 seconds left after Detroit trailed 3-0, then the Kraken won the shootout 4-3.

items.headline: Draisaitl's two power-play goals lift Edmonton over Minnesota in overtime
items.summary: The Oilers won 4-3; Kaprizov had a goal and an assist and Eriksson Ek put 8 shots on goal for the Wild.

items.headline: Lamar Jackson still day-to-day with his ankle
items.summary: Baltimore hasn't confirmed whether he'll face Cincinnati; Tyler Huntley has started the last two games.

items.headline: Two games tonight: Flyers at Sabres and Panthers at Senators
items.summary: Vladar, Luukkonen and Schmid are confirmed and Ullmark is likely; Ottawa's Ullmark (.945) is the best goalie on the slate.

fantasyWeeks.method: For each defense I computed PPR points allowed per game to each position from season box-score totals (QB: 0.04/pass yd, 4/pass TD, −2/INT, 0.1/rush yd, 6/rush TD). Dividing by the league average gives a matchup factor. With only five games per team, I shrink each factor halfway toward 1.00, then multiply it by the player's season PPR average to project this week.
fantasyWeeks.notes: Matchup factor 1.20 means the defense has allowed about 20% more than average after shrinking for sample size. Lamar Jackson is out (Tyler Huntley starts), so he is off the QB list; Hurts and Mayfield are also out, which lowers the Eagles' and Buccaneers' passing games without changing their opponents' matchup grades.
